hits.tldr: Grant postgres user ownership of custom database roles to fix db push permission errors.
Run a shell script to reassign database object ownership from supabase_admin to postgres.
Comment out supabase_admin OWNER lines in schema.sql to resolve permission errors.
Database ownership error occurs when supabase_auth_admin role loses table privileges.
Deploy schema migrations to remote Supabase instances using `supabase db push` with optional seed data.

structuredContent.text:
### Permission denied on `db push`

If you create a table using a custom database role, the default `postgres` user may lack permission to modify it. This can cause `42501` privilege errors during migrations. To resolve this, grant the 'postgres` user ownership of the custom role.

```sql
grant "custom_role" to "postgres";
```

structuredContent.text:
### Step 1: Update database object ownership

Use the provided script to reassign ownership of database objects in the `public` schema from `supabase_admin` to `postgres`. From the project directory containing `docker-compose.yml`, run:

```sh
sh utils/reassign-owner.sh
```

<Admonition type="note">

This script only updates ownership for database objects in the `public` schema. Supabase-managed and custom schemas are not affected.

</Admonition>

content.text: Don't switch the CLI to `supabase_admin` — the docs recommend instead granting `postgres` ownership of whatever role created the table, e.g. `grant "custom_role" to "postgres";` (apps/docs/content/guides/deployment/managing-environments.mdx, "Permission denied on db push"). A `GRANT ALL` won't fix this since ownership, not privileges, is what's checked. If it's specifically `supabase_admin`-owned public-schema objects (self-hosted), use the ownership-reassignment script instead: `sh utils/reassign-owner.sh` (apps/docs/content/guides/self-hosting/remove-superuser-access.mdx, "Step 1: Update database object ownership").
